title: Register for, collect and file the meals (food and beverage) tax
question: My restaurant, caterer or store sells prepared food. How do I collect and file Staunton's meals tax?
summary: Every restaurant, caterer, coffee shop, convenience store or grocery deli in Staunton must register with the Commissioner of the Revenue and add the city's 7% meals tax to prepared food and drinks, on top of the 5.3% state sales tax. First get the health permit and a city business license. Each month, fill in the Meals Tax Return and send it with a check payable to the City of Staunton, Treasurer, to the Commissioner by the 20th of the following month. Filing and paying on time lets you keep a 3% seller's discount. Paying late costs a 5% penalty plus 10% a year interest. State law exempts tips, grocery food and some other sales.

steps.step: Check that your business and sales are covered by Staunton's meals tax
steps.who: Business owner (restaurant, caterer, coffee shop, convenience store, grocery deli, food truck or other seller of prepared food or drinks in the city)
steps.how: The city says every business located in Staunton that sells meals or beverages must collect the tax. State law keeps some sales out of it: tips (and mandatory service charges up to 20 percent), factory-sealed alcohol sold to take away, grocery 'food' other than sandwiches, salad-bar items, single-serving salads and non-sealed drinks, vending-machine sales, SNAP and WIC purchases, free employee meals, meals paid for by a government, qualifying nonprofit fundraisers, and small farmers-market sellers (up to $2,500 a year). The tax follows the place of business, not where the food is delivered.
steps.quote: Every restaurant, caterer, coffee shop, convenience store, grocery deli, etc. located in the City of Staunton engaged in the business of selling meals and/or beverages

steps.step: Get the health permit from the Staunton-Augusta environmental health office
steps.who: Business owner; Virginia Department of Health, Central Shenandoah Health District (Staunton-Augusta Environmental Health)
steps.how: For a new or remodelled food service establishment or a new mobile food unit, send the Plan Review Application with its fee to the local health department (food trucks use the Mobile Unit Plan Review Application, form f6). Once the plan review is approved, send the Foodservice Permit Application with its fee. A change of owner also needs a new application. The VDH page names the Foodservice Permit Application but does not link it, so ask the office for the form.
steps.deadline: Foodservice Permit Application at least 30 days prior to opening
steps.fee: $40.00 application fee for the plan review; $40.00 application fee for the foodservice permit
steps.quote: Once a Plan Review is approved, submit a completed Foodservice Permit Application, along with a $40.00 application fee, at least 30 days prior to opening for approval.

steps.step: Apply for a Staunton business license, with the health permit attached
steps.who: Business owner; Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: Mail, fax or email the Business License Application to the Commissioner of the Revenue. Attach the health permit, zoning approval (or Home Occupation Permit) and any SCC registration or fictitious-name filing, and enter your Virginia sales tax number on the application. Selling alcohol also needs a Virginia ABC license and adds an ABC license tax. This is modelled in full in the separate bpol_business_license process.
steps.deadline: Within 30 days of when you begin to conduct business (the city's Start a Business page); state law says to apply before beginning business (Va. Code § 58.1-3703.1(A)(2)(a)), so apply before opening
steps.fee: Minimum $30.00 for gross receipts of $0-$50,000; above that, a rate by classification (see the application)
steps.quote: The health permit must be included with the business license application.

steps.step: Register with the Commissioner of the Revenue as a meals tax collector
steps.who: Business owner; Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: The city requires every seller of meals to register with the Commissioner of the Revenue. No separate meals tax registration form is published, so ask the office (by phone, by email or at City Hall) how to register. No registration deadline is published; lexflow suggests asking when you apply for the business license, before your first taxable sale. Food trucks must register in each locality where they sell.
steps.quote: engaged in the business of selling meals is required to register with the Commissioner of Revenue, collect the tax and file the appropriate returns.

steps.step: Charge the 7% meals tax on each taxable sale and hold it for the city
steps.how: Add Staunton's 7% meals tax to the price of taxable prepared food and beverages. It is on top of the 5.3% Virginia retail sales tax, which is filed with Virginia Tax, not the city. Meals tax you collect is held in trust for the city; wrongful and fraudulent use of it is embezzlement (§ 58.1-3833(B)), and willfully failing to collect, account for or pay over the tax is a Class 1 misdemeanor (§ 58.1-3907(A)).

steps.step: Fill in the Meals Tax Return for the month
steps.how: Use the printable Meals Tax Form or the fillable Meals Tax Form Interactive. Enter the tax year and month, trade and corporate names and mailing address. Line 1: the month's gross receipts from taxable meals and beverages. Line 2: deductions for free employee meals, meals paid for by a federal, state or local government, and any other deduction with an explanation. Line 5 is 7% of net receipts. Line 6 takes a 3% seller's discount off the tax, but only if you file and pay on time (tick the box). Sign and date the return.
steps.fee: Tax: line 4 x 7%; seller's discount: line 5 x 3%, only when filed and paid on or before the due date
steps.quote: Sellers Discount only applies if return is filed and paid on or before the due date.

steps.step: File the return and pay the tax by the 20th of the following month
steps.who: The business; Commissioner of the Revenue (receives the return); City Treasurer (payment)
steps.how: Send the signed return with a check made payable to 'City of Staunton, Treasurer' to the Commissioner of the Revenue, P.O. Box 4, Staunton, VA 24402. The Commissioner's office is in City Hall, 1st floor, 116 W. Beverley St., but the form does not describe filing in person, so ask. The form's office-use box has a 'Paid at Treasurer' entry, which suggests you can also pay in person at the Treasurer's Office. The city's online and phone payment services list only real estate, personal property and utility bills, so no online meals tax payment was found.
steps.deadline: On or before the 20th day of the month following the tax month. If that day is a Saturday, Sunday, legal holiday or a day the office is closed, the return and payment may be filed the next business day (Va. Code § 1-210(E); the city's Taxes page says the same for payments)
steps.quote: To avoid penalty and/or interest, this return with payment must be filed on or before the 20th day of the month following the tax month.

steps.step: If the return or payment is late, add the penalty and interest
steps.who: The business; Commissioner of the Revenue and City Treasurer
steps.how: A late return loses the 3% seller's discount. Add the 5% late-payment penalty (line 8) and interest at 10% a year (line 9), and enter the total on line 10. State law caps the penalty on meals tax that is collected but not sent in: 10% for the first month, 5% for each month after, up to 25% (or $10 if that is greater, but never more than the tax). State law says penalty and interest shall not be imposed if the lateness was not your fault, or if you can show proof of timely mailing; ask for them to be removed (see escalation).
steps.deadline: From the day after the due date
steps.fee: Penalty: line 7 x 5%; interest: 10% per annum

steps.how: Keep register, point-of-sale and deduction records behind each monthly return. If the Commissioner finds local tax that was not assessed, or was assessed too low, for any of the three preceding tax years, the Commissioner shall assess it with penalty and interest (if that was through no fault of yours, penalty and interest run only from 30 days after the assessment). Willfully using a device or software to falsify point-of-sale records, or otherwise manipulating transaction records that affect a local tax, is a Class 1 misdemeanor and carries a $20,000 civil penalty (§ 58.1-3907(B) and (C)). City Code § 3.40.060 covers keeping records; its text was not read.
steps.quote: If the commissioner of the revenue of any county or city or the tax-assessing officer of any town ascertains that any local tax has not been assessed for any tax year of the three preceding tax years

steps.step: Tell the Commissioner when you close or sell the business
steps.who: Business owner; Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: Notify the Commissioner of the Revenue in writing that you have stopped operating, with the closing date and your signature. Meals tax collected in your last month of sales is still due on the monthly return by the 20th of the following month. The city's pages do not describe a final meals tax return, so ask the office.
steps.quote: In order to close your business license, you must notify our office in writing that you have ceased to operate your business and provide a closing date and a signature.

escalation.trigger: A meals tax assessment is believed wrong (for example an assessment of omitted tax under § 58.1-3903, deductions or exempt sales disallowed, or a math error)
escalation.next: Commissioner of the Revenue: written application for correction of the assessment
escalation.deadline: Within three years from the last day of the tax year, or within one year from the date of the assessment, whichever is later
escalation.quote: may, within three years from the last day of the tax year for which such assessment is made, or within one year from the date of the assessment, whichever is later, apply to the commissioner of the revenue or such other official who made the assessment for a correction thereof

escalation.trigger: The correction application is filed within 90 days of the assessment
escalation.next: Collection pauses: the assessment is not treated as delinquent while the application is pending and for 30 days after the decision (interest may still be charged on any amount found due)
escalation.deadline: Application filed within 90 days of the date of the assessment
escalation.quote: so long as the appeal is filed within 90 days of the date of the assessment, and for 30 days after the date of the final determination of the appeal

escalation.trigger: The Commissioner denies the application, or grants only part of it
escalation.next: Commissioner of the Revenue: ask for a written statement of the facts and law behind the decision, mailed to you
escalation.quote: if so requested by the applicant, the commissioner or other such official shall state in writing the facts and law supporting the action on such application

escalation.trigger: Tax was overpaid because of an erroneous assessment
escalation.next: Refund of the excess by the City Treasurer. Under § 58.1-3981(A), City Council directs the refund on the Commissioner's certificate, with the City Attorney's consent, that the assessment was erroneous (Council may let the Treasurer approve refunds up to $10,000). Under a refund ordinance allowed by § 58.1-3990, the Commissioner certifies the erroneous amount to the Treasurer, who refunds it with any penalties and interest paid. City Code § 3.55.010 covers refunds of local taxes erroneously paid; its text was not read, so which route Staunton uses is not confirmed.
escalation.deadline: Correction route: three years from the last day of the tax year, or one year from the assessment, whichever is later (§ 58.1-3980); refund-ordinance route: no refund if the application is made more than three years after the last day of the tax year (§ 58.1-3990)
escalation.quote: direct the treasurer of the county, city or town to refund the excess to the taxpayer

escalation.trigger: The Commissioner agrees the assessment is improper or an obvious error but cannot correct it under § 58.1-3981
escalation.next: The Commissioner applies to the Staunton Circuit Court for relief on the taxpayer's behalf
escalation.quote: the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official shall apply to the appropriate court, in the manner herein provided for relief of the taxpayer

escalation.trigger: Still aggrieved after the Commissioner's decision, no decision (no state deadline for deciding a meals tax correction application was found), or choosing to go straight to court
escalation.next: Staunton Circuit Court, with the City of Staunton as the named party (heard by a judge, no jury; the taxpayer carries the burden of proof)
escalation.deadline: Whichever is latest: three years from the last day of the tax year, one year from the assessment, or one year from the Commissioner's final determination under § 58.1-3981
escalation.quote: apply for relief to the circuit court of the county or city wherein such assessment was made

caveats: The City of Staunton's website (www.ci.staunton.va.us) refuses automated readers, so the city pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The Local Tax Forms page was last copied on 2026-02-15 and the meals tax PDFs on 2025-10-14. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them or by phone before you act.

Local law not checked. The City Code page now leads to General Code's eCode360. Its terms limit content to personal use and forbid reproducing it for public purposes. Only the Title 3 table of contents has been checked, for Chapter 3.40 (Tax on Meals Served in Restaurants or by Caterers, §§ 3.40.010 to 3.40.080) and the section links; descriptions in the citations paraphrase the headings. The older codepublishing.com copy refuses automated readers. So the rate, due date, seller's discount, penalty, interest, record-keeping rule, definitions and local exemptions were not checked against the ordinance. All local rules here come from the city's Meals Tax Return, Taxes page, Start a Business page and brochure.

Who is covered. The chapter heading names restaurants and caterers. The city's pages also name coffee shops, convenience stores and grocery delis. How the ordinance defines a taxable meal or a covered seller was not read. State law (§ 58.1-3840(B)) bars a city from taxing grocery 'food' except sandwiches, salad-bar items, single-serving salads and non-sealed drinks.

Registration. No meals tax registration form is on the Local Tax Forms page, and no page says how or by when to register. Whether registration happens through the business license application, a separate form or a call is not stated. No registration fee is stated. Ask the Commissioner of the Revenue.

Food trucks and outside vendors. State law (§ 58.1-3715.1(C)) requires a mobile food unit owner to register with the commissioner of the revenue in every locality where it sells. The city's pages say nothing about food trucks, event vendors or businesses based outside the city. Under § 58.1-3841 the tax follows the place of business. How Staunton applies it to trucks based elsewhere was not confirmed.

Filing details not stated. The form is monthly, and no quarterly or annual option was found. The pages do not say whether a return is required for a month with no taxable sales, whether returns may be emailed (the form prints the office email but says to submit return and payment to P.O. Box 4), or whether cash or cards are accepted in person. The Treasurer's online and phone payments are listed only for real estate and personal property taxes and utility bills, and so are their service-provider fees (2.35% by card for the two taxes, $2.25 per card payment for utilities, $0.25 per eCheck).

Weekend rule. The Taxes page says payments due on a day the office is closed are accepted the next business day without penalty. Va. Code § 1-210(E) goes further: an act that state law or a local ordinance requires on a Saturday, Sunday, legal holiday or a day the office is closed may be done on the next business day, which covers filing the return as well as paying.

Penalty and interest come from the city's return, not from ordinance text: 5% of the tax for late payment and 10% a year interest. Both are within the state caps in § 58.1-3916. The return states no separate late-filing penalty and does not say when interest starts or whether the 5% recurs monthly.

Seller's discount. The 3% discount for timely filing and payment is on the city's return. Its ordinance basis was not read. A search of the Virginia Code index found no statute that sets a meals tax dealer discount. § 15.2-1104 lets a municipal corporation set a discount for early payment of taxes by ordinance, and may be the general authority, but this was not confirmed. The 3 to 5 percent commission in § 58.1-3819(D) is for lodging tax, not meals tax.

Deductions. The return lists only free employee meals and government-paid meals, plus an 'Other (please provide explanation)' line. State exemptions are wider (gratuities, factory-sealed alcohol, grocery food, vending, SNAP and WIC, qualifying nonprofit fundraisers, schools, hospitals, day care centers and others under § 58.1-3840). Reporting them on the 'Other' line is this page's reading of the form; whether exempt sales belong in line 1 at all is not stated.

Legal hints. §§ 58.1-3819 and 58.1-3826 govern the transient occupancy (lodging) tax and are not used here. § 58.1-3833(A) is the county food and beverage tax (capped at 6 percent) and does not apply to an independent city like Staunton. Only subsection B is used: it preserves existing city meals tax authority and makes meals tax collections a trust. No state cap on a city's meals tax rate was found in § 58.1-3840. That section's authority depends on the city's charter taxing powers; the Staunton Charter was not read.

Appeal route. § 58.1-3983.1 (90-day determinations, appeals to the State Tax Commissioner, written rulings) covers only 'local business tax' as defined there: machinery and tools, business tangible property, merchants' capital and some consumer utility tax. The BPOL route under § 58.1-3703.1 is for license tax only. Neither covers meals tax. So the route here is a correction application to the Commissioner (§ 58.1-3980), then the circuit court (§ 58.1-3984). No state deadline for the Commissioner to decide was found, no advisory-ruling procedure for meals tax was found, and no city page on meals tax appeals was found. Circuit court filing fees are not covered here.

License refusal. § 58.1-3700(A) lets a city refuse a business license until delinquent meals taxes are paid. The city's Business License Application mentions only delinquent business license and personal property taxes. Whether Staunton withholds licenses for unpaid meals tax was not confirmed.

Health permit. The Business License Application Instructions link a VDH food-services page that returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-11. The current Central Shenandoah Environmental Health page is cited instead. The two VDH plan review PDFs are 21-page and 13-page packets with no fillable fields. The page names the Foodservice Permit Application but does not link it. Virginia ABC licensing and the city's ABC license tax are not covered here.

Contacts. The Treasurer's phone line (540-332-3833) is published for help with real estate and personal property tax payments, so it is not listed for meals tax. City forms and pages print the names of elected officers; they are not recorded here.

Refunds. Whether Staunton refunds through the § 58.1-3981 correction route, a § 58.1-3990 refund ordinance (City Code § 3.55.010, not read) or both, and whether City Council has let the Treasurer approve refunds up to $10,000, was not confirmed.

corrections: Quotes: all 49 original state-law quotes are in the indexed text of the sections they cite (lexflow check_quotes: 49 of 49; the verifier also read each one in context to check subsection letters and meaning). All 29 city and VDH quotes were found word for word, spacing aside, in copies the verifier fetched again: the Internet Archive copies named in sources for the city pages and PDFs (the live city site still answers HTTP 403, robots.txt included), and the live VDH pages. The 4 state-law quotes added below are confirmed the same way (final file: 53 state-law quotes matched by check_quotes, 29 local quotes confirmed).

s9: the step said the Commissioner "can" assess omitted tax; Va. Code § 58.1-3903 says the Commissioner "shall" assess it, with penalty and interest, and that penalty and interest run only from 30 days after the assessment when it was through no fault of the taxpayer. Reworded.

s9: "Altering point-of-sale records is a crime" overstated § 58.1-3907(B), which covers willfully using a device or software to falsify cash-register or point-of-sale records, or otherwise manipulating transaction records that affect a local tax (a Class 1 misdemeanor; the $20,000 civil penalty is in subsection C). Reworded and added a § 58.1-3907(B) legal_basis quote.

s5: added that willfully failing to collect, account for or pay over the tax is a Class 1 misdemeanor (§ 58.1-3907(A), already quoted), and tied the embezzlement statement to the statute's words (wrongful and fraudulent use, § 58.1-3833(B)).

Escalation rung 4 (refunds): the rung said the Commissioner certifies and the Treasurer refunds. Under § 58.1-3981(A) the governing body directs the refund on the Commissioner's certificate with the city attorney's consent (or lets the Treasurer approve refunds up to $10,000); under a § 58.1-3990 refund ordinance the Commissioner certifies to the Treasurer, who refunds with penalties and interest paid, and no refund is made on an application more than three years after the last day of the tax year. Rewrote next and deadline, set type to refund, added two legal_basis quotes (§ 58.1-3990 three-year limit, § 58.1-3981(A) $10,000) and a Refunds caveat.

Weekend due date: added Va. Code § 1-210(E) (an act required by state law or local ordinance on a Saturday, Sunday, legal holiday or office-closed day may be done the next business day) as a legal_basis quote; s7's deadline and the weekend caveat now say it covers filing the return as well as paying, which the caveat had left as an assumption.

s8 and the state-cap fee entry: § 58.1-3916 caps the meals penalty at 10% for the first month and 5% a month after, up to 25%, or $10 whichever is greater, never more than the tax; the $10 floor was missing. s8 also now says state law bars penalty and interest when the lateness was not the taxpayer's fault or timely mailing is proven ("shall not be imposed"), rather than a waiver to ask for.
Escalation rung 1: the example "an estimated assessment made because no return was filed" had no source; replaced with an assessment of omitted tax under § 58.1-3903.

Form f2: the fillable return's scripts calculate lines 3 to 7 and 10 (the 3% discount only when its box is ticked); penalty and interest (lines 8 and 9) are typed in. The title said it calculates lines 4 to 10. Corrected.

Forms f5 and f6: the verifier opened both VDH plan review PDFs (21 and 13 pages); neither has fillable fields, so fillable is false, and the health permit caveat no longer says they were not opened. s2 now names the mobile unit form f6 and notes that the VDH page names the Foodservice Permit Application without linking it. Three sources added.

s3: the Virginia sales tax number is entered on the license application, not attached (the instructions say sales tax numbers must be included on the application). s4: the advice to ask before the first taxable sale is now marked as lexflow's suggestion, since no registration deadline is published. s10: the final-month return is now stated as the monthly return still due by the 20th, not as a separate requirement.

Checked and unchanged: the eCode360 Title 3 table of contents (robots.txt allows it; only headings read) matches every City Code citation (Chapter 3.40, §§ 3.40.010 to 3.40.070, 3.05.090, 3.55.010; § 3.40.080 is Interpretation of ordinance). The Local Tax Forms page links both meals forms at the cited URLs; f1 has no form fields; the PDF creation dates match. Contacts (Commissioner office, phone, fax, office mailbox, P.O. Box 4, Treasurer office and drop box, VDH Staunton-Augusta Environmental Health, Staunton Circuit Court Clerk's Office) match the cited pages. No staff names or personal mailboxes are recorded. Step and form ids are unique and every referenced form exists.
open_issues: The city site (www.ci.staunton.va.us) still refuses the research client (HTTP 403, robots.txt included, re-checked 2026-10-11), so every city quote is confirmed only against Internet Archive copies (forms page 2026-02-15, meals tax PDFs 2025-10-14, Taxes page 2026-08-22). This does not change any step, but the live pages should be confirmed.

Staunton City Code Chapter 3.40 text was not read (eCode360 terms forbid reproducing it for public purposes; only the table of contents was read). The 7% rate, the 20th-of-the-month due date, the 3% seller's discount, the 5% penalty and the 10% interest rest on the city's official return and pages, not the ordinance; how the ordinance defines a taxable meal, whether it imposes a separate late-filing penalty, and its record-keeping period are unknown.

Not stated on any page read: how and by when a new seller registers for meals tax, any registration fee, whether a zero-sales month needs a return, whether returns may be emailed or filed in person, and how food trucks or sellers based outside the city are handled. The steps say to ask the office; they do not invent an answer.

No state deadline for the Commissioner to decide a meals tax correction application, and no state basis for the 3% seller's discount, were found (§ 15.2-1104's early-payment discount may be the general authority; not confirmed). Which refund route Staunton uses (§ 58.1-3981 or a § 58.1-3990 ordinance) and whether the Treasurer may approve refunds up to $10,000 were not confirmed.

Not researched: circuit court filing fees, Virginia ABC licensing and the city's ABC license tax, and whether Staunton withholds a business license for unpaid meals tax (§ 58.1-3700(A) allows it; the application mentions only business license and personal property taxes).
